title: Armed Man Arrested After Charging at Ohio Democratic Gubernatorial Candidate Amy Acton
meta_title: Armed Man Arrested After Charging at Candidate Amy Acton
meta_description: An armed man was arrested after charging toward Democratic Ohio governor candidate Amy Acton at the Canfield Fair, injuring several people in the crowd.
discover_titles: Armed Man Arrested After Charging Toward Ohio Candidate Amy Acton at Fair
Chaos at Canfield Fair: Armed Suspect Tackled While Rushing Toward Amy Acton
Amy Acton Security Stops Armed Man Charging Ohio Democratic Campaign Tent
spot: An armed suspect carrying two pistols and brass knuckles was arrested Sunday after charging toward Democratic Ohio gubernatorial nominee Amy Acton at the Canfield Fair, injuring multiple bystanders before security subdued him.
content_html:
Key Developments

An armed man was taken into custody on Sunday after violently rushing toward Democratic candidate for Ohio governor Amy Acton during a campaign appearance at the Canfield Fair. While Acton was not injured, campaign officials and local authorities reported that multiple bystanders suffered injuries during the confrontation.

Mahoning County Sheriff Jerry Greene identified the suspect as 38-year-old Patrick Havas of Canfield, Ohio. According to Greene, Havas aggressively shoved his way through the crowd toward Acton while holding up a mobile phone. As he charged forward, Havas allegedly knocked over two older individuals riding mobility scooters, causing one person to tumble to the ground.

Wayne Penny Jr., a Democratic candidate running for Ohio's 59th State House District, witnessed the incident at the Democratic Party's tent. Penny reported that hecklers had assembled near the booth when one individual bull-rushed through the gathering, knocking down volunteers and toppling an elderly man with Parkinson's disease, who struck his head on the ground. Mahoning County Democratic Party Chairman Chris Anderson confirmed that several campaign volunteers were knocked down.

Acton's personal security detail acted quickly to stop Havas, restraining him until local law enforcement arrived to take him into custody. Authorities found that Havas was carrying two handguns and a set of brass knuckles, weapons that are legal to carry under Ohio law. Havas was booked into the Mahoning County Jail and faces one count of disorderly conduct and two counts of misdemeanor assault.

Key Takeaways

  • Patrick Havas, 38, was arrested after charging toward Democratic candidate Amy Acton at the Canfield Fair while holding a cell phone.
  • The suspect was armed with two pistols and brass knuckles, and multiple attendees—including an elderly man with Parkinson's—were injured when shoved to the ground.
  • Acton's security detail subdued the suspect without injury to the candidate, and Havas is facing assault and disorderly conduct charges.

Why It Matters

The altercation highlights escalating security concerns surrounding public campaign stops in high-profile political races. Acton, the state's former public health director, is currently running in a competitive race for governor against Republican nominee Vivek Ramaswamy. Campaign communications director Addie Bullock condemned the confrontation, stating that Dr. Acton remains grateful for the swift response of law enforcement and that political violence has no place in the state. Ramaswamy also denounced the episode on Sunday as unacceptable, emphasizing that political candidates must be able to engage directly with voters without facing violence or disruption.
